status: declared by the pull request that closes #1265 before any score was computed; a development study, never a verdict. (s3c) stays the H5 candidate until Eleonora rules on the result. Nothing is registered or published: no record in docs/runs/ is edited, the live record and its pin do not change, no declaration already merged changes, docs/research/h5-candidate.json, `gbm_funding`'s declaration, `scripts/final_test_preregistration.py` and metadata/sources.json do not change, no day after 2026-09-03 is read and no lockbox day is scored. Amendments made after a number was computed are listed in `amendments`; there are none.
ruling: Eleonora, 27 October 2026, about 1:15 pm ET, chat, relayed on #1265: option 1 on finding #1261, which takes in avenue #1264.
hypothesis: H5 (primary goal): the SOFR - IORB spread distribution in bp. Step 3, the candidate (s3c). Development tier
target: spread_bps at the scored day, in basis points, as a 23-quantile distribution at each lead h = 1..5 (scoring_protocol.GRID)
why: at full allotment (s3c) caps every quantile at the SRF line (IORB + 10 bp, margin 0), and the event is read as 1 - F(10.5), so P(SOFR - IORB > +10 bp) is at most about 1% and exactly 0 when q97.5 and q99 sit on the line. SOFR closed above the line on 26, 29 and 31 December 2025 (+11, +12 and +22 bp; #1252). Decision days 24 to 30 December 2025 fall in neither of #1255's scored windows.

candidate.label: (s3c-t)
candidate.definition: (s3c) with the cap off on turn days: on a target day whose reporting type is `year_end`, `quarter_end_turn` or `turn` the quantiles are (s3)'s, unclipped; on every other day (s3c) exactly (cap at the line at full allotment, margin 0 bp, (s3) itself before full allotment). A transform of (s3)'s forecast quantiles after the walk; it fits nothing
candidate.module: repo_model.s3c_turn_cap (is_turn, capped_quantiles); the cap, the line and the full-allotment flag are repo_model.s3c_candidate's and repo_model.srf_line's, unchanged
candidate.turn_day: the reporting type of the target day under the day types in force: turn_days.reporting_day_type, read at the target day from the date and the market holiday table, as the calendar columns are (asof rule 2). A label that is not one of turn_days.LABELS raises ValueError, never read as 'not a turn'; the legacy reading (--legacy-day-types) is not offered
candidate.pairs: direct: (s3) reads the calendar columns at the target day with training_pairs = 'direct' (as in #1255); the provisional-register row is metadata/provisional/cleared/s3c_turn_cap_1265.json

frame.decision_days: every decision day from 2025-12-10 whose five targets all fall on or before 2026-09-03 (the near-blind tier open since GO #151, metadata/lockbox.json), in one contiguous frame, so that 24 to 30 December 2025 are scored. The walk of (s3) is the one of #1229 and #1255 (all decision days from the start of the panel, refit every 21 decision days, direct pairs), so (s3) is the same forecast on a day both studies score; only the days scored differ
frame.guards: a scored decision day or target day passes lockbox.require_unlocked through spread_mean_reversion_686.require_scored_days with the last day 2026-09-03; the blind tier (from 2026-09-04) and every lockbox day are refused
frame.reproduction: (s3), (s3c), B1, B1' and B2 on the decision days from 2025-12-31 are #1255's 2026 window exactly; the pooled means on those days are compared with docs/research/s3c-candidate-1255/result.json and the difference stated on the page

arms.name: sc_s3c_turn
arms.role: (s3c-t), (s3c) with the cap off on turn days

primary.metric: grid CRPS (23 levels) averaged over leads h = 1..5
primary.pressure_probability: the Brier score of P(spread > +5 bp) and of P(spread > +10 bp) (docs/decisions/pressure-probability.md), each probability read off the 23 quantiles as 1 - F(floor(tau) + 0.5), F linear between them (spread_mean_reversion.exceedance), the event strict and on whole basis points (data.exceeds_bp)
primary.comparisons: (s3), (s3c) and (s3c-t) paired with each other and against B1, B1' and B2

scoring.scorer: repo_model.scoring_protocol (#655), the development tier: no verdict, no registration
scoring.test: scoring_protocol.paired_tests, the studentized stationary bootstrap (ruling 1), mean block 10 business days, 10,000 draws, seed 1265, two-sided 90% interval (the lower end is the one-sided 95% bound); the skill interval and the studentized interval on mean d are reported for every tested row; where the studentized bound cannot be computed the unstudentized percentile interval of mean d is given beside it, with no reading taken from it
scoring.reading: a reading is taken from the mean-d bound (her ruling on #1009): the later arm is read better than a reference when the lower end of the 90% interval of mean d is above zero, worse when the upper end is below zero, otherwise undecided. Lens C's caveat (the lag-10 HAC standard error is understated about 2x after 2020) is stated on the page
scoring.splits: pooled; by lead; by turn day and other days (the target day's reporting type is a turn or not); by pressure-day type of the target day; by target month; the decision days of 24 to 30 December 2025 (means only: a group of fewer than 20 days is listed and not tested). The intervals of a group of target days keep the current method (the group's days, scattered, resampled in date order as if consecutive), which #1221 questions and #1228 will decide
scoring.identical_groups: a group in which an arm's score equals the reference's on every day is listed as identical and not tested against it

event_list: every target day in the scored frame on which SOFR - IORB closed above +5 bp or above +10 bp (strict, whole basis points), with the realised spread, the day's reporting type, and each model's P(> +5) and P(> +10) at each lead h = 1..5 whose decision day is scored, as docs/decisions/pressure-probability.md lists events. The counts of positive days and cells are in result.json
bounds_check: the highest P(> +10 bp) of (s3c) over the cells at full allotment, and the number of cells where it is exactly 0, reported with the same figures for (s3) and (s3c-t), so that the page states (s3c)'s bound from the figures
reading_rules: A figure is a check on days that were already seen. Nothing here is a verdict, nothing is registered and no choice is made on it; (s3c) stays the candidate until she rules on the result.
A gain or loss is read from the 90% interval of mean d excluding zero; otherwise undecided. A point estimate alone is not read.
A pooled figure is never read without the turn-day, other-day and month splits beside it. The pressure figures rest on few days; the page states the counts.
The page says plainly: at full allotment (s3c) gives P(> +10 bp) of at most about 1% by construction, and 0 when the upper quantiles sit on the line.
The page ends with marked questions for Eleonora with numbered options and defaults that change no claim.
